content_units: Best Fit for an Engineering Student
Given your priorities—  battery life first, then light gaming, then MATLAB/CAD  , all under   $1,300  —the best overall pick is   C  , followed closely by   B   and   A  .
Context note: Option   D   is over budget, so it is treated as a trade-off alternative rather than a valid main recommendation.
Ranked Laptop Comparison
Rank   Option   Price   Why it ranks here

1     C       $1,149     Best balance for engineering school:   32GB RAM   is excellent for MATLAB, multitasking, and larger technical workloads; still portable with   11-hour battery  . Weakest point is integrated graphics, so gaming and heavier 3D CAD are limited.

2     B       $1,279     Best performance under budget for   gaming and CAD   thanks to   RTX 4050   and 1TB SSD. Strong all-rounder, but   7-hour battery   and   1.9 kg   weight make it less ideal for all-day campus use.

3     A       $1,099     Best for portability and battery:   1.2 kg   and   14 hours   are excellent for classes. Ryzen 7 + 16GB is solid for MATLAB and general engineering work, but integrated graphics limits gaming and more demanding CAD/3D work.
4     D       $1,399     Most powerful option with   Ryzen 9 + RTX 4060  , but it is   over your $1,300 budget  , heavy at   2.3 kg  , and has weak battery life for student use.
Why This Ranking Fits Your Priorities
Option C — Best overall for student life
-   Best for MATLAB and heavy multitasking   because   32GB RAM   matters a lot in engineering workflows.
-   11-hour battery   is strong enough for long campus days.
-   1.4 kg   is still very portable.
- Main trade-off: integrated graphics means only   light gaming at modest settings   and less headroom for GPU-accelerated CAD/3D work.
Option B — Best if gaming/CAD matter more
-   RTX 4050   makes this the strongest in-budget option for   light gaming, 3D modeling, and GPU-assisted CAD tasks  .
-   1TB SSD   is great for project files, software installs, and games.
- Trade-offs:   heavier   and battery life is much worse for lectures, labs, and studying away from outlets.
Option A — Best battery-first budget choice
- If you care most about   mobility and battery life  , this is very attractive.
- Ryzen 7 + 16GB is enough for   typical MATLAB, coding, reports, and general engineering coursework  .
- It falls behind   C   because 16GB is less future-proof, and behind   B   because no dedicated GPU.
Option D — Performance-first, but not practical here
- Great raw specs, but it breaks the budget and is the least student-friendly to carry daily.
- Worth considering only if you can exceed budget and need stronger 3D/CAD or gaming performance.
Final Buying Recommendation
If you want the   smartest overall university choice  , pick   Option C  .
If you want the   best gaming/CAD performance under budget  , pick   Option B  .
If you want the   lightest and longest-lasting laptop for campus  , pick   Option A  .
